steps.look: imageGCHighThresholdPercent and low. Defaults of 85 and 80 are too tight on nodes running large images.

steps.title: Cordon the node while you work
steps.look: The node shows SchedulingDisabled.
steps.note: Marks the node unschedulable so nothing new lands while you clear space. Running pods are unaffected, but capacity elsewhere must absorb new work. Remember to uncordon afterwards or the node stays out of the pool permanently.

causes.cause: Too many images cached on the node.
causes.fix: Lower the GC thresholds, and shrink your images. Both help.

causes.cause: Container logs filled the disk.
causes.fix: Set containerLogMaxSize and containerLogMaxFiles in the kubelet config.

causes.cause: A pod wrote large files to its writable layer.
causes.fix: Set ephemeral-storage limits so one workload cannot fill the node.

causes.cause: The node disk is simply too small.
causes.fix: Resize, or use a node type with more storage for image-heavy workloads.

verify: DiskPressure is false.
No new evictions.
GC thresholds and log rotation are configured.
escalate: GC thresholds in the kubelet config

title: Cluster does not add nodes for pending pods
summary: Pods stay Pending and no new node appears.

steps.title: Read the autoscaler's decision
steps.look: It logs why it did or did not scale. That log is the answer; everything else is inference.

signals.means: The pool is already at its ceiling.
The pod would not fit on a new node of any available type.
No pool satisfies the pod's selectors or tolerations.

steps.title: Check the pod's requests against node capacity
steps.look: A request larger than any node type can provide means no amount of scaling will help.

steps.title: Check the pod's scheduling constraints
steps.look: The autoscaler only scales pools the pod could actually use. A selector matching no pool is invisible to it.

steps.title: Check pool limits
steps.look: Which pools exist and how many nodes each has. Compare against the configured maximum.

causes.cause: The node pool is at its maximum size.
causes.fix: Raise the maximum. The autoscaler will not exceed it.

causes.cause: The pod is larger than any node type.
causes.fix: Reduce the request, or add a larger node type.

causes.cause: No pool matches the pod's constraints.
causes.fix: Label a pool to match, or relax the selector.

causes.cause: The cloud account is at its instance quota.
causes.fix: Raise the quota. The autoscaler reports the provider's refusal.

causes.cause: The pod uses local storage, which blocks scale-down but also confuses placement.
causes.fix: Check the autoscaler's safe-to-evict annotations.

verify: A new node appears and the pod schedules.
The autoscaler log shows a successful scale-up.
escalate: Autoscaler log lines for this pod

title: HTTPS fails on an ingress
summary: Browsers warn, or clients reject the certificate the ingress serves.

steps.title: See which certificate is served
steps.look: The issuer tells you immediately whether a real certificate or the controller's placeholder is being served.

signals.means: The controller's placeholder. Your TLS secret is missing or not found.
Compare the date against now. Expired means renewal stopped.

steps.title: Check the ingress references a secret
steps.look: The secretName and the hosts it covers. The secret must live in the same namespace as the ingress.

steps.title: Check the secret exists and has both keys
steps.look: tls.crt and tls.key must both be present. A secret of the wrong type is ignored silently.

steps.title: Check cert-manager issued it
steps.look: READY False carries a message. ACME challenges failing on HTTP-01 usually means the ingress is not reachable from outside.

causes.cause: The TLS secret does not exist in this namespace.
causes.fix: Create it there. Secrets do not cross namespaces.

causes.cause: The certificate expired.
causes.fix: Renewal stopped. Check cert-manager rather than just reissuing by hand.

causes.cause: The certificate does not cover the requested host.
causes.fix: Add the host to the certificate's SAN list and to the ingress tls hosts.

causes.cause: The ACME challenge cannot complete.
causes.fix: HTTP-01 needs the ingress publicly reachable on port 80. Use DNS-01 for private clusters.

causes.cause: The secret is not type kubernetes.io/tls.
causes.fix: Recreate it with the right type.

verify: The correct certificate is served.
It is valid for the host and not near expiry.
Renewal is automated.
escalate: Subject, issuer and dates from openssl

title: A resource keeps reverting to an old state
summary: You change something and it changes back within seconds.

steps.title: Watch the resource version change
steps.look: Rapidly incrementing with nobody editing means a controller is writing continuously.

steps.title: Check for controller ownership
steps.look: Every manager that has written to this object. Two managers owning the same field is the whole problem.

signals.means: A GitOps controller owns it. It will revert anything not in Git.
An autoscaler owns replicas.

steps.title: Check annotations naming an owner
steps.look: GitOps tools record their source here. That tells you where the real change belongs.

steps.title: Check for an operator managing it
steps.look: An owner reference means a higher-level resource controls this one. Editing the child is always futile.

causes.cause: A GitOps controller reverts drift.
causes.fix: Change it in Git. That is the tool working correctly.

causes.cause: An HPA owns the replica count.
causes.fix: Remove replicas from your manifest so the two do not fight.

causes.cause: An operator owns the object.
causes.fix: Edit the custom resource, not the generated object.

causes.cause: Two pipelines deploy the same workload.
causes.fix: Pick one owner. This is an organisational fix, not a technical one.

verify: The change persists.
Only one controller owns each field.
escalate: Which managers have written to the object

title: kubectl commands are very slow
summary: Every command takes many seconds even for simple reads.

steps.title: Time a trivial request with verbose output
steps.look: The round trip time. Throttling messages name the client-side rate limiter rather than the server.

signals.means: The client is rate-limiting itself, not the server.
Seconds for a health check means the server is genuinely slow.

steps.title: Check how large the responses are
steps.look: Thousands of objects means every list is expensive. Namespace-scoped queries are far cheaper.

steps.title: Check the discovery cache
steps.look: A stale or missing cache forces rediscovery on every command, which is slow on clusters with many CRDs.

steps.title: Check control plane health
steps.look: Each check individually. A failing etcd check explains cluster-wide slowness better than anything client-side.

causes.cause: The client rate-limits itself.
causes.fix: Raise --request-timeout and QPS, or scope queries to a namespace.

causes.cause: The discovery cache is stale.
causes.fix: Delete the cache directory. It rebuilds on the next command.

causes.cause: Cluster-wide lists are expensive.
causes.fix: Query by namespace and label. Avoid -A in scripts.

causes.cause: The API server or etcd is under load.
causes.fix: A cluster-level problem. Check etcd latency metrics.

causes.cause: High latency to the endpoint.
causes.fix: Check the path, especially over VPN.

verify: Commands return promptly.
No throttling messages.
Control plane checks pass.

title: Pods land on the wrong nodes
summary: Workloads schedule onto nodes they should not use, such as expensive or spot instances.

steps.title: See where the pod actually landed
steps.look: The NODE column, then check that node's labels. Placement is only as good as the constraints you declared.

steps.title: Read the pod's placement constraints
steps.look: Empty means the scheduler was free to pick anything. Preferred affinity is a hint, not a rule.

signals.means: A preference, not a requirement. The scheduler may ignore it entirely.
No constraints at all. Any node is fair game.

steps.title: Check the target nodes are labelled
steps.look: The label must exist on the nodes you want. A pool replaced by the autoscaler often loses custom labels.

steps.title: Check spread constraints are satisfiable
steps.look: A spread constraint across zones needs nodes in each. With whenUnsatisfiable DoNotSchedule the pod stays Pending instead.

causes.cause: The pod declares no placement rules.
causes.fix: Add nodeAffinity or a nodeSelector for the intended pool.

causes.cause: Affinity is preferred rather than required.
causes.fix: Use requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution if it genuinely must hold.

causes.cause: Target nodes lack the label.
causes.fix: Label them, ideally through the node pool definition so replacements inherit it.

causes.cause: Other workloads also land on the dedicated pool.
causes.fix: Taint the pool so only tolerating pods can use it. Affinity alone does not exclude others.

causes.cause: Topology spread cannot be satisfied.
causes.fix: Check nodes exist in every topology domain.

verify: Pods land on the intended nodes.
Other workloads are excluded from dedicated pools.
escalate: Labels and taints on the target nodes

title: Custom resource is not recognised
summary: Applying a custom resource fails because the kind is unknown.

steps.title: Read the apply error
steps.look: No matches for kind names the kind and apiVersion that could not be resolved. Both matter.

signals.means: The CRD is absent, or the apiVersion is wrong.
Applying resources before the CRD that defines them.

steps.title: Check whether the CRD exists
steps.look: Present means the definition is installed. Absent means the operator was never installed or was removed.

steps.title: Check the served versions
steps.look: Your apiVersion must be one that is served. An old version can exist but be disabled after an operator upgrade.

steps.title: Refresh the local discovery cache
steps.look: kubectl caches API discovery. A CRD installed seconds ago may not appear until the cache refreshes.

causes.cause: The CRD is not installed.
causes.fix: Install the operator or chart that defines it, first.

causes.cause: Resources applied before their CRD.
causes.fix: Apply CRDs first. Use sync waves in GitOps.

causes.cause: The apiVersion is no longer served.
causes.fix: Update the manifest to a served version.

causes.cause: The discovery cache is stale.
causes.fix: Delete ~/.kube/cache/discovery.

causes.cause: The CRD exists elsewhere.
causes.fix: Check your context.

verify: The custom resource applies.
kubectl api-resources lists the kind.

title: Image pull works for one namespace but not another
summary: The same image pulls fine in one place and fails elsewhere.

steps.title: Compare pull secrets between namespaces
steps.look: Pull secrets are namespaced. Working elsewhere means the secret exists there and not here.

steps.title: Check the ServiceAccount carries it
steps.look: Attaching the secret to the ServiceAccount applies it to every pod using that account, which is usually cleaner than per-pod.

signals.means: The ServiceAccount has no pull secret attached.

steps.title: Check the pod's own reference
steps.look: A pod-level secret overrides nothing but adds to the ServiceAccount's. Either path works; neither existing does not.

steps.title: Verify the secret's contents are valid
steps.look: Base64 of the registry config. A secret created with the wrong type is ignored silently by the kubelet.

causes.cause: No pull secret in this namespace.
causes.fix: Create it here. Secrets never cross namespaces.

causes.cause: The ServiceAccount has no pull secret.
causes.fix: Patch it onto the ServiceAccount so all its pods inherit it.

causes.cause: The secret is not dockerconfigjson.
causes.fix: Recreate with kubectl create secret docker-registry.

causes.cause: The registry token in the secret expired.
causes.fix: Rotate it. Cloud registry tokens are often short-lived.

causes.cause: Every new namespace needs this by hand.
causes.fix: Use a controller that replicates the secret, or bake it into namespace provisioning.

verify: The image pulls in this namespace.
New pods inherit the secret automatically.

title: CronJob runs at the wrong time of day
summary: The schedule fires hours away from when you expected.

steps.title: Read the schedule and any timezone
steps.look: An empty timeZone means the controller's own zone, which is UTC on nearly every cluster.

signals.means: No timezone set. The schedule is interpreted in UTC.
A timezone is set. Confirm the cluster version supports it.

steps.title: Check when it last fired
steps.look: The timestamp is UTC. Compare against your local expectation to confirm the offset explains it.

steps.title: Check the cluster version supports timeZone
steps.look: spec.timeZone is stable from 1.27. On older clusters it is silently ignored, which looks like it did nothing.

steps.title: Check for daylight saving effects
steps.cmd: kubectl get cronjob {job} -n {namespace} -o yaml | findstr schedule
steps.look: A UTC schedule does not shift with local clock changes, so a job pinned to local business hours drifts by an hour twice a year.

causes.cause: The schedule is interpreted in UTC.
causes.fix: Set spec.timeZone, or express the schedule in UTC deliberately and document it.

causes.cause: The cluster ignores timeZone.
causes.fix: Upgrade, or convert the schedule to UTC by hand.

causes.cause: Local business hours shift twice a year.
causes.fix: Set timeZone so the controller handles the transition.

causes.cause: The controller's zone is not UTC.
causes.fix: Unusual but possible. Check the controller manager's configuration.

verify: The job fires at the intended local time.
It still does after a daylight saving change.

title: Pod evicted for filling emptyDir
summary: A pod using scratch space fills the node's disk and gets evicted.

steps.title: Read the eviction message
steps.look: It names ephemeral-storage and usually the container that exceeded it.

signals.means: The pod exceeded its local storage allowance.
An emptyDir volume grew past its limit.

steps.title: Check whether limits are declared
steps.look: Without an ephemeral-storage limit the pod can consume the node's whole disk and take other workloads down with it.

steps.title: Check the emptyDir definition
steps.look: An emptyDir with no sizeLimit is unbounded. A medium of Memory consumes RAM rather than disk, which is a different failure.

steps.title: Check what is filling it
steps.look: The directories consuming space. Logs written to files rather than stdout are the usual cause.

causes.cause: No ephemeral-storage limit is set.
causes.fix: Set a request and limit so the pod is evicted before the node fills.

causes.cause: The emptyDir has no sizeLimit.
causes.fix: Set one. The pod is then evicted rather than the node filling.

causes.cause: The app writes logs to disk.
causes.fix: Log to stdout. The platform handles rotation.

causes.cause: emptyDir medium is Memory.

title: Traffic reaches the wrong pods
summary: Requests to one service land on another workload's pods.

steps.title: See which pods back the service
steps.look: The pod names. Anything unexpected here means the selector is matching more than intended.

steps.title: Read the selector
steps.look: A broad selector such as a single app label matches every workload carrying it, including other versions.

signals.means: A single-label selector. Broad enough to catch unrelated pods.

steps.title: Find every service using overlapping labels
steps.look: Two services with the same selector both receive the same pods, which is legal and almost never intended.

steps.title: Check the pods' labels
steps.look: Which pods carry the matching labels. A canary or an old ReplicaSet still labelled the same way is the usual culprit.

causes.cause: The selector matches more pods than intended.
causes.fix: Add a version or component label so each service targets exactly its own workload.

causes.cause: Pods from an old ReplicaSet still match.
causes.fix: They should have been removed. Check the rollout completed.

causes.cause: A canary shares the selector.
causes.fix: Give the canary a distinguishing label and a separate service.

causes.cause: A service was copied and the selector not updated.
causes.fix: Fix the selector. This is the most common origin.
